title: Settings export: verification plan
subtitle: Manual verification run for `settings-export`
intro: Manual pass for exporting and importing app settings as a JSON file. Results go in the **Status** columns and the run log. Findings that change a decision go back to the proposal.
scope:
Before merge: export writes a complete, readable file on both platforms, import restores it, and a failed write never leaves a half-written file behind.

Out of scope: the settings schema itself (covered by unit specs) and cloud sync.

covered.what: Serialise/parse round trip, schema version check
Export button writes a file in a temp dir

coveredGap: Nothing exercises the real OS save dialog, a destination another process holds open, or the packaged build's file paths.
setup: Build the packaged app on each platform from the branch head. Keep a copy of the settings file so the destructive case can be undone.

risks.R1: The native save dialog returns a path the export code doesn't expect (sandboxed or bookmarked path on macOS)
risks.R2: Overwriting a file another process holds open fails, and the error isn't shown
risks.R3: Import of a file from an older version silently drops settings

items.title: Build the packaged app (Linux)
items.why: Packaged paths differ from dev; the dialog and file writes must be tested on the real build.

steps.t: Build and launch the packaged app.

expect: The app opens to the home screen

items.title: Build the packaged app (macOS)
items.why: Same as SL1, on the Mac checkout.

steps.cmd:
git fetch origin && git switch settings-export && git pull
npm ci

steps.t: Build, then open the app from Finder.

expect: The app opens to the home screen

items.title: Export through the save dialog
items.why: The OS dialog is the only path users take, and no spec drives it.

steps.t: Settings → **Export settings…** → save as `settings.json` on the Desktop. Record the full path below.

expect: A toast says the settings were exported

items.title: Overwrite a file that's open elsewhere
items.why: Overwrite behaviour on an open file differs by OS; a silent failure loses the user's export.

steps.t: Open `{{A1.path}}` in a text editor and leave it open.
Export again to the same path and confirm the overwrite.

expect: Either the file is replaced, or an error names the file
No `settings.json.tmp` is left on the Desktop

items.title: Import an export from the previous release
items.why: Version migration is the riskiest part of import; this records what survives.

steps.t: Compare the preferences screen with the fixture's values.

exit.text: Every required case has a status
Every ✗ is fixed or deferred with a reason
